title: Statistics - Lesson 10: Conclusions from Position Measures Assessment
description: Assessment for drawing conclusions from quartiles, percentile rank, IQR, and statistical displays.

questions.question: Which statement best describes an evidence-based conclusion from position measures?
options: It cites a statistic such as median, quartile, IQR, or percentile rank and explains what it means in context.
It gives the largest value and ignores the rest of the data.
It chooses the answer that sounds most positive.
It reports a number without mentioning the group.
questions.explanation: An evidence-based conclusion must use a relevant statistic and interpret it in the original situation.

questions.question: For the ordered data 12, 15, 18, 22, 26, 30, 33, what is the median?
questions.explanation: There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value, 22.

questions.question: For the ordered data 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, what are Q1 and Q3?
questions.explanation: The median is 18. The lower half is 10, 12, 15, so Q1 = 12. The upper half is 20, 22, 25, so Q3 = 22.

questions.question: A data set has Q1 = 18 and Q3 = 43. What is the IQR? Enter just the number.
The IQR describes the spread of the middle half of the data, not the full range.
questions.explanation: IQR uses Q3 - Q1, so it focuses on the middle 50% of values.

questions.question: A learner scored 88. In a group of 25 learners, 21 scored at or below 88. Which interpretation is best?
options: The learner is at about the 84th percentile, so the score is as high as or higher than about 84% of the group.
The learner earned 84% on the test.
The learner answered 21 questions correctly.
The learner is below most of the group.
questions.explanation: 21/25 x 100 = 84, so the percentile rank is about 84. This is relative standing, not necessarily percent correct.

questions.question: Class X has Q1 = 58 and Q3 = 82. Class Y has Q1 = 64 and Q3 = 76. Which class has the more consistent middle half, and why?
options: Class Y, because its IQR is 12 while Class X's IQR is 24.
Class X, because its Q3 is higher.
Class X, because its IQR is larger.
Both are equally consistent because both have quartiles.
questions.explanation: Class X has IQR 82 - 58 = 24. Class Y has IQR 76 - 64 = 12. A smaller IQR means more consistency in the middle half.

questions.question: A box plot for Section A has median 72 and IQR 18. A box plot for Section B has median 70 and IQR 8. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: Section A has a slightly higher median, but Section B has a more consistent middle half.
Section B is higher in every possible way.
Section A is more consistent because 18 is larger than 8.
No conclusion can mention spread from a box plot.
questions.explanation: The median compares typical values, while IQR compares middle-half spread. Section A's median is higher, but Section B's IQR is smaller.

questions.question: If Q1 = 20, Q3 = 36, and IQR = 16, what is the upper fence using Q3 + 1.5(IQR)? Enter just the number.
A score of 90 and the 90th percentile always mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: A score is a data value. A percentile rank describes relative standing compared with a group.

questions.question: A report says, 'The new strategy helped because the maximum score increased from 86 to 96.' What is the best critique?
options: A maximum is only one value; the report should also compare medians, quartiles, IQR, or sample details.
The maximum is always the best measure of typical performance.
The conclusion is automatically proven because 96 is larger than 86.
Quartiles cannot be used to compare groups.
questions.explanation: A single maximum does not show what happened to the group overall. More position measures would make the claim stronger.

questions.question: A data set has Q1 = 25, median = 31, and Q3 = 37. Write one sentence interpreting these values if the data represent minutes of exercise.
questions.correctAnswer: The middle half of the group exercised from 25 to 37 minutes, with a median of 31 minutes.
questions.explanation: A good answer should name the middle-half interval and connect it to exercise minutes.

questions.question: Explain why a box plot is useful when comparing two classes' test scores.
questions.correctAnswer: A box plot shows median, quartiles, spread, and possible extremes, so it helps compare both typical score and consistency.
questions.explanation: The explanation should mention that box plots show more than one statistic, especially median and IQR.

questions.question: Class A has median 81 and IQR 20. Class B has median 79 and IQR 6. A principal wants the class with the more consistent scores. Which class should be chosen, and why?
questions.correctAnswer: Class B should be chosen for consistency because its IQR is 6, much smaller than Class A's IQR of 20, even though Class A has a slightly higher median.
questions.explanation: Consistency is about spread, so IQR is the key evidence. The answer should not ignore the median, but the smaller IQR supports Class B.

questions.question: In your own words, describe the difference between calculating a position measure and drawing a conclusion from it.
questions.correctAnswer: Calculating a position measure finds a value such as a quartile, median, IQR, or percentile rank. Drawing a conclusion explains what that value means for the data group and question.
questions.explanation: A complete response should separate computation from interpretation and mention context.
